This working context summary is non-authoritative and exists only to orient later audit tasks. The corpus describes Turnix as a platform/specification set around packs/mods, runtime hosting, activation, state/memory, RPC, UI/views, adapters, jobs, permissions, tracing, audit/replay, and documentation governance. Major documentation families are CORE META-RULES, DESIGN DOCTRINE, DESIGN AREA, OPTIONAL DESIGN AREA, and IMPLEMENTATION SPECIFICATION. Major architectural areas include platform core boundaries, pack discovery and identity, activation and lifecycle, services/capabilities/permissions, AppInstance/ApplicationRun runtime identity, RPC channels/transports, frontend views, adapters/code runtimes, orchestration/mutation authority, runtime host/workspace/command surfaces, catalog/pack management, ModCallContext invocation, and trace/audit schemas. Obvious terminology clusters include pack-root/content-root/root-system terms; run/lifecycle terms; service/capability/permission/policy terms; RPC/channel/transport/message terms; host/workspace/client/command terms; and trace/window/audit/export terms. Major naming uncertainties noticed include AppInstance versus ApplicationRun/Application, runtime host versus host/client instance, adapter entry/pack entry/cyclic activation/standalone runtime terms that appear less established, and Turnix naming mixed with generic implementation terms.
